text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them or vouches for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- Serbian parliament adopts special law on recognition of local electin results, appoints 13 new ministers and forms three new ministries. Seven ministers relieved of their duties and one ministry, for private enterprise, abolished.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno continues protest gatherings until entry into force of the new law on local elections and says real fight for democratisation of Serbia lies ahead.
- Serbian parliament strips current Belgrade mayor Nebojisa Covic from his parliamentary mandate.
- Nat West Markets official says it is too early for sale of shares of Serbia's PTT in response to Financial Times report on Italian firm Stet buying 49 percent of the Serbian postal firm's shares.

- Some 1,800 out of Serbia's 2,200 schools are on strike, Teachers' trade unions still waiting to be received by government announce more puiblic protests. Parents also announce protest gathering to support of teachers' demands and urge their speedy fulfilment.

- Victory in Serbia's bigger towns gives opposition chance to slowly start winning media over. Opposition already has media in Nis and Kragujevac and could soon gain Belgrade TV station Studion B, commentary.
- Yugoslav embassy in Athens protests to Greek daily To Vima that it tailored President Slobodan Milosevic's interview given to the paper in written form.
- Opposition leader Vesna Pesic nominated for Nobel peace prize by the International peace Bureau.
- Montenegrin railway blocks 4,000 tonnes of products of Smederevo's Sartid Steel works in Bar because of the latter's 13 million dinar debt.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President meets U.N. Eastern Slavonia administrator Jacques Klein. They agree it is necessary to create conditions for equal participaton of all citizens in upcominig local elections in the region.
- Assistant of international coordinator Sir Arthur Watts denies any knowledge about setting up an arbitration commission for the succession of former Yugoslavia.
- January exports up 42.7 percent and imports 39.7 percent on same month in 1996, says statistical office.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Some 20,000 people protested peacefully in Vukovar demanding the eastern Slavonia region remain single territory.

- Seidi Veseli says in an interview from Tirana to Albanian language paper Zeri he is heading the National Committee for Liberation of Kosovo which is fighting for liberation of Kosovo from Serbia by armed action.

- No bank has gone into recievership because of only three days of deficit on its accounts, but for more long-term insolvency, says deputy governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Bozidar Gazivoda.
POLITKA EKSPRES
- Three men rob a taxi driver at gunpoint in yet another in a series of attacks and killings of Belgrade taxi drivers.
BORBA
- Federal government proposes that Borba daily becomes public firm, says federal information secretariat.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 43 05
